questions.question: A Grade 4 class in Kelowna has 96 pencil crayons. The teacher shares them equally among 3 supply bins, so every bin gets the same number. How many pencil crayons go in each bin?
questions.explain: Break 96 into 90 and 6: 90 ÷ 3 = 30 and 6 ÷ 3 = 2, so each bin gets 30 + 2 = 32. A common trap is writing the digits in the wrong order and answering 23 — always check by multiplying back: 3 × 32 = 96.

questions.question: Mei has 72 markers. She keeps taking away 6 markers at a time to make groups of 6, and she stops when there are 0 markers left. How many equal groups of 6 does she make?
questions.explain: Repeated subtraction counts how many times you take the group size away: 6 × 10 = 60 leaves 12, and 12 is 2 more sixes, so 10 + 2 = 12 groups. A common trap is subtracting 6 only once and answering 66 — you must keep subtracting until nothing is left.

questions.question: A librarian has 150 books and puts exactly 5 books on each shelf. She works in big chunks: she takes away 50 books (that is 10 shelves), then another 50 books (10 more shelves), then the last 50 books (10 more shelves), and 0 books are left. How many shelves does she fill?
questions.explain: With partial quotients you add up the number of groups, not the number of subtractions: 10 + 10 + 10 = 30 shelves. A common trap is counting the three chunks and answering 3 — each chunk was worth 10 shelves.

questions.question: Sam has 47 marbles. He shares them into 4 equal groups and keeps any marbles that are left over. How many marbles are in each group, and how many are left over?
questions.explain: Take away 4 × 10 = 40, leaving 7; 7 holds one more four, so 11 in each group with 3 left over. A common trap is stopping at 10 groups with 7 left over — if the leftover is still as big as the divisor, you can make another group, so the remainder must be smaller than 4.

questions.question: Use partial quotients to find 375 ÷ 5. Which answer is correct?
questions.explain: Subtract 5 × 70 = 350, leaving 25, and 25 is exactly 5 more fives, so the quotient is 70 + 5 = 75. A common trap is stopping too soon and answering 70 r 25 — a remainder must always be smaller than the divisor.

questions.question: Ravi finds 156 ÷ 6 like this: 156 − 60 (that is 10 sixes) = 96, then 96 − 60 (10 more sixes) = 36, then 36 − 36 (6 sixes) = 0. What is 156 ÷ 6?
questions.explain: Add the number of sixes taken out each time: 10 + 10 + 6 = 26, and 6 × 26 = 156 checks it. A common trap is adding the amounts subtracted instead of the group counts (10 + 10 + 36) and answering 56.

questions.question: Mrs. Chan spends $174 on 6 identical hoodies for the school choir. Each hoodie costs the same amount. How much does one hoodie cost?
questions.explain: Take out 6 × 20 = 120, leaving 54, and 54 ÷ 6 = 9, so 20 + 9 = $29 each. A common trap is losing one of the tens and answering $19 — check with 6 × 29 = 174.

questions.question: A rectangular vegetable plot at a community garden has an area of 245 square metres. One side of the plot measures 5 m. How long is the other side?
questions.explain: Area ÷ one side = the other side, so 245 ÷ 5: take out 5 × 40 = 200, leaving 45, and 45 ÷ 5 = 9, giving 40 + 9 = 49 m. A common trap is stopping after the first chunk and answering 40 m, or subtracting 5 instead of dividing and answering 240 m.

questions.question: 138 students from a Surrey school are going to Science World. Each van can carry 8 students, and every student must ride. What is the smallest number of vans the school needs?
options: 17 vans, and 2 students are left behind
questions.explain: 138 ÷ 8 gives 17 with 2 left over (8 × 17 = 136), and those 2 students still need a ride, so you round up to 18 vans. A common trap is answering 17 and ignoring the remainder — always ask what the leftover means in the story.

questions.question: Liam has $92 saved. He spends $20 on a book at the school book fair, then shares the money that is left equally among his 4 younger cousins. How much does each cousin get?
questions.explain: Subtract first, then divide: 92 − 20 = 72, and 72 ÷ 4 = 18 (4 × 10 = 40, leaving 32, and 32 ÷ 4 = 8, so 10 + 8 = 18). A common trap is dividing $92 by 4 and answering $23, which forgets the book he bought.

questions.question: Ava works out 216 ÷ 4 with partial quotients. She subtracts 4 × 50 = 200, leaving 16, then subtracts 4 × 4 = 16, leaving 0. She writes her answer as 50 + 16 = 66. What is the correct quotient?
questions.explain: In partial quotients you add the number of groups you pulled out, so 50 + 4 = 54, and 4 × 54 = 216 proves it. Ava's mistake is adding the amount she subtracted (16) instead of the 4 groups it stood for.

questions.question: A tree-planting crew on Vancouver Island has 618 seedlings to share equally among 6 volunteers, with none left over. How many seedlings does each volunteer plant?
questions.explain: Take out 6 × 100 = 600, leaving 18, and 18 ÷ 6 = 3, so each volunteer gets 100 + 3 = 103. A common trap is dropping the middle zero and answering 13 — 6 × 13 is only 78, far too small, so estimating first tells you the answer must be near 100.
